headline: Highest risk is medium: Mentat can write shared files and modify git state, while python-cheatsheet is read-only documentation, so prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks are limited but not zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat can read/write filesystem and modify git state, so if python-cheatsheet content is manually copied into Mentat, malicious instructions could be followed. python-cheatsheet itself has no execution or file-write surface, so the bridge is manual and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF the operator copies python-cheatsheet text into Mentat prompts or files
IF Mentat is asked to treat copied documentation as instructions
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet content out of prompt text unless quoted as data
Use a separate notes file for pasted reference material
Ask Mentat to summarize before acting on pasted content
Review diffs before accepting any edit
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for pasted snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code files and can send prompts to a configured model provider, but python-cheatsheet has no filesystem, clipboard, or API surfaces. There is no direct shared data channel in the profiles, so leakage is limited to manual transfer of code or notes.
conditions: IF source code from Mentat is manually pasted into python-cheatsheet-related notes
IF the operator exports Mentat outputs into a shared document
mitigations: Avoid pasting secrets into either agent
Use redacted snippets when sharing outputs
Store code and notes in separate folders
Check model-provider settings before sending Mentat prompts
requires-engineering: enforce workspace segregation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, while python-cheatsheet is non-runnable and read-only. The conflict is one-sided, but if both are pointed at the same repo or workspace, Mentat can overwrite files that python-cheatsheet content references, creating default shared-state contention via filesystem.
conditions: IF both are used against the same working tree or shared directory
IF Mentat commits or rewrites files that the reference content points to
mitigations: Use separate directories for code and reference material
Pause Mentat before editing shared files
Review git diffs before commit
Lock the workspace during edits
requires-engineering: add file-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces edit proposals from source files, and python-cheatsheet is a reference artifact that could be treated as authoritative by a human or workflow. If python-cheatsheet-derived guidance is fed into Mentat without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes, though python-cheatsheet itself does not act on outputs.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet text is used as the basis for coding decisions
IF Mentat edits are accepted without human review
mitigations: Verify reference claims against primary docs
Ask Mentat for rationale before applying edits
Test changed code locally
Require human review of diffs
requires-engineering: add citation checks to the workflow

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is identified for either agent: Mentat only touches source code in selected files, and python-cheatsheet touches no data classes. There is no documented residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the shared workflow
IF the operator routes PHI or EU PII through either agent
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use synthetic examples for testing
Review data-handling policies before deployment
